item.title: Connectivity and Diameter of Friends and Strangers Graphs Using Minimum Degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.20648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given graphs $X,Y$ on $n$ vertices, Defant and Kravitz defined the friends and strangers graph, denoted $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$. The vertices of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ are bijections $\sigma:V(X)\to V(Y)$, and two bijections $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ are adjacent in $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ if they differ by a transposition $(ab)$ such that $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $X$ and $\sigma(a)$ and $\sigma(b)$ are adjacent in $Y$. Our main result resolves a conjecture of Bangachev that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs and $2\min\{\delta(X),\delta(Y)\}+3\max\{\delta(X),\delta(Y)\}\ge 3n$, then $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is connected. The main step in the proof is showing that there exists an absolute constant $C$ such that for any adjacent vertices $a,b\in V(X)$ and any vertex $\sigma\in V(\mathrm{FS}(X,Y))$, $a$ and $b$ can swap positions in at most $C$ moves. Furthermore, we prove that if $X,Y$ are connected graphs satisfying the above minimum degree condition, then the diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2/\min\{\delta(X),\delta(Y)\})$, and that this is sharp as a bound on the maximum diameter of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ in this regime. This work improves the diameter results of Akella and Li, and resolves many of their questions. Moreover, we show that even for disconnected graphs $X$ and $Y$, the same minimum degree condition implies that the diameter of any connected component of $\mathrm{FS}(X,Y)$ is $O(n^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Kai Mawhinney

item.title: Cotangent cohomology and higher-order obstructions of matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.20649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that matroid Stanley-Reisner rings can have essential deformation obstructions of arbitrarily high order over every field, even at corank three. For every $m\ge3$, we construct a connected cosimple matroid with $m$ fine-homogeneous first-order deformation classes whose proper subcollections integrate jointly and whose pairwise primary cup products vanish. These classes define a joint flat family whose $(m-1)$-jet has no lift to order $m$, even without preserving the grading. For the duals of rank-three truncations of $U_{2,m}\oplus U_{2,n}$, $m,n\ge3$, every nonzero homogeneous class modulo the primary cup image is realized as a higher-order obstruction, and this quotient has an explicit module presentation with $m+n-2$ minimal homogeneous generators. The construction is based on a computation of the full multigraded second cotangent cohomology $T^2$ and its primary cup image in terms of flats and parallel classes of the dual matroid. This computation also proves that $T^2$ vanishes precisely when every connected component has corank at most two, equivalently when the matroid has no $U_{1,4}$-minor, settling the conjecture of Constantinescu, Klein, Nguyen, Singh, and Venturello. The same criterion characterizes formal smoothness of the affine deformation functor.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang

item.title: The $A^A$ problem for finite ordered sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.20817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For ordered sets $X$ and $Y$, let $Y^X$ denote the ordered set of order-preserving maps from $X$ to $Y$, ordered pointwise. In 1984, D. Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ forces $A\cong B$ when $A$ and $B$ are finite ordered sets. We prove that it does. The proof combines direct decompositions with an auxiliary ordering of connected ordered sets and a careful choice of intervals of maximum height. We then extend the reconstruction result to several forms of repeated exponentiation.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan David Farley, George Gr\"atzer

item.title: Path Covering Spaces of Posets
item.description: arXiv:2610.20890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we extend results concerning a kind of covering space for finite posets that bears some analogy to the topological theory of covering spaces. Previous work focused on ranked, locally-finite posets with a unique minimal element. In this previous work the notion of a covering space based on preservation of path weights was defined, and it was shown that, given a poset, there is a unique universal covering space which has an explicit description. Numerous examples of combinatorially significant posets and their universal covers were explored. In this paper we consider finite posets that have a unique minimal element, but that need not be ranked. We give a combinatorial description of these covering spaces, which we call path covers. We then show these covers naturally form a supersolvable lattice and deduce some of its properties. Finally, we investigate an analogue of deck transformations and give some results relating these transformations, poset automorphisms, and the automorphisms of the lattice of path covers.
item.dc:creator: Matteus Froese, Ian George

item.title: Crossing numbers of simplicial complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies crossing numbers of $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes drawn in $\mathbb R^{2d}$ or $\mathbb S^{2d}$. We clarify and generalize a number of known results and conjectures from the graph case to higher dimensions: the crossing lemma (including the exceptional case of two-dimensional complexes drawn in dimension $4$), a generalized Harary-Hill conjecture (and evidence for it), existence of a midrange crossing constant (in a weak sense), and upper bound constructions based on stochastic geometry (related to Sylvester's problem) and the cyclic polytope. Some of our results are new even in the case of graphs: we give a simple proof of the Harary-Hill conjecture for antipodal drawings, and sharpen the threshold above which the rectilinear and spherical crossing numbers of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph behave like those of the complete graph.
item.dc:creator: Alfredo Hubard, Cheikh Saliou Ndiaye, Oriol Sol\'e-Pi

item.title: Linear bounds for rich-neighbor edge-colorings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An edge in a proper edge-coloring is rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. A rich-neighbor edge-coloring is a proper edge-coloring in which every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. The rich-neighbor chromatic index $\rn(G)$ is the minimum number of colors in such a coloring. We prove that every loopless multigraph $G$ satisfies $\rn(G)\le3\chi'(G)$, where $\chi'(G)$ is the chromatic index. Exact values are also determined for complete bipartite graphs and complete graphs. For all positive integers $m,n$, $\rn(K_{m,n})=m+n-1$, except that $\rn(K_{2,2})=4$. For $n\ge3$, $\rn(K_n)=2n-3$, except that $\rn(K_4)=6$ and $\rn(K_6)=10$. Moreover, for $n\ge7$, the rich edges in every optimal rich-neighbor edge-coloring of $K_n$ form a star forest.
item.dc:creator: Jiangxu Kong

item.title: Coefficient lifting for skew divided differences and triple Schubert coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.21053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skew divided difference operators \(\partial_{w/v}\), introduced by Macdonald, play an important role in the study of Schubert polynomials and their structure constants. For permutations \(u,v,w\in S_n\), we show that the coefficient of each monomial \(\xx^\alpha\) in \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\), where \(\SSch_u(\xx;\yy)\) is the double Schubert polynomial, is a single triple Schubert coefficient evaluated at \(\tb=0\), whose indices form an explicit lift of \((u,v,w)\) to \(S_{n+\abs{\alpha}}\). As an application, we show that every coefficient of \(\partial_{w/v}\SSch_u(\xx)\) is a single Schubert structure constant. This gives a new proof of Kirillov's conjecture that these coefficients are nonnegative.
item.dc:creator: Byung-Hak Hwang

item.title: Decomposing multigraphs into two Class I subgraphs with prescribed maximum degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.21097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite loopless multigraph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $\chi'(G)=\Delta+k$, where $k\ge0$. We prove that for every pair of positive integers $p,q$ satisfying $$p+q=\Delta+k\qquad\text{and}\qquad p,q\le\Delta,$$ the graph $G$ admits an edge decomposition into two spanning Class I subgraphs $H_p,H_q$ with $$\Delta(H_p)=p \qquad\text{and}\qquad \Delta(H_q)=q.$$
item.dc:creator: Yonglei Chen, Yan Cao

item.title: Local modifications in planar hypohamiltonian graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for $n \geq 36$ there exists a planar hypohamiltonian graph of order $n$. As a corollary, we prove that for $n \geq 33$ there exists an almost hypohamiltonian planar graph of order $n$. Further, we exhibit over 100 planar hypohamiltonian graphs of order less than 40, including new graphs of orders 36, 37, 38, and 39. The proof utilizes three local modifications that alter a graph $G$ by removing a subgraph $H$ and replacing it with $H'$ to form a new graph $G'$: a plus two modification, a plus three modification, and Thomassen's iterable plus four modification. The plus two modification preserves hypohamiltonicity in general, and the plus three modification preserves hypohamiltonicity in our cases of interest. This establishes the main result beginning with Tsai's order 34 examples. Further, we conjecture that among planar hypohamiltonian graphs, Tsai's 34 vertex examples are the smallest order. The conjecture is based on previous results, constraints on the degree modulo 3, and experimentation with planar graphs consisting entirely of 4-gons and 5-gons.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Durias, Sabrina Guerrero, Briana Jaiyen, Daniel Kaplan, Austin Lapine, Caleb Peralta, Akul Shrivastav

item.title: Strong Lefschetz property of the Kirchhoff algebra of the complete tripartite graph $K_{1,1,n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By Whitney's 2-isomorphism theorem, the cycle matroids of two graphs are isomorphic if and only if one graph can be transformed into the other by finitely many applications of two operations: separation or identification at a cut-vertex, and twisting. The complete tripartite graph whose vertex set is the disjoint union of two singletons and an $n$-element set is invariant, up to isomorphism, under these operations. In this paper we prove that the Macaulay inverse system (the Kirchhoff algebra) determined by the basis generating polynomial of the cycle matroid of such a graph has the strong Lefschetz property over a field of characteristic $0$. The proof reduces the non-degeneracy of the higher Hessians to the ranks of disjointness matrices of families of subsets (the Gottlieb--Wilson theorem) and to the representation theory of the symmetric group in relation to the Johnson scheme.
item.dc:creator: Yohji Akama

item.title: The Rate of the Delsarte Bound for Binary Codes and Spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.21263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give the asymptotic rate of Delsarte's linear programming bound for binary codes and spherical codes. This extends previous work of the author which formulated and proved an analogue of the conjecture of Afkhami-Jeddi, Cohn, Hartman, de Laat, and Tajdini for binary codes, obtaining the rate of the Delsarte linear program at distance $1/2-1/\pi$. The lower bounds introduce ideas from potential theory into the study of Delsarte's bounds, whereby the measures underlying a system of orthogonal polynomials give an obstacle problem. We solve the resulting obstacle problem in the case of binary codes and spherical codes, obtaining a closed form for the lower bound in terms of elliptic integrals. For the upper bounds, we relate the $N$-qubit construction for binary codes used in previous work of the author to the constructions in OpenAI's Chapter 2 for spherical codes and observe that they both involve interlacing spectra. This leads to a variational problem involving measures constructed from these spectra under the Markov-Krein correspondence. This variational problem admits an exact solution and matches the lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Salmon

item.title: Local Extrema and Infinite Derivatives of the Delange Function of Base 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.21265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the ternary Hamming cube $Q_n^3$, the smallest number $\xi_n(m)$ of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices is $2(nm-S_3(m))$, where $S_3(m)=\sum_{j<m}s_3(j)$ and $s_3$ is the ternary digit sum. After rescaling, these numbers are the values at the points $m/3^n$ of a continuous function $T$ of Takagi type, the Delange function of base $3$. Both facts are known. In this paper, we study the local structure of $T$. The local minima of $T$ are exactly the ternary rationals, that is, the numbers $m/3^n$ with integers $m$ and $n\ge0$. The local maxima are exactly the points $(m+1/2)/3^n+k$, where $k$, $m$ and $n$ are integers with $n\ge0$, $0\le m<3^n$ and $s_3(m)=n$. We also characterize the points $x$ where $T$ has an infinite derivative from one or both sides, in terms of their ternary digits $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$. At a ternary rational the derivative is $+\infty$ from the right and $-\infty$ from the left. At every other point, the derivative from the right is $+\infty$ exactly when the digit slopes $2\sum_{j\le n}(1-\xi_j)$ tend to $+\infty$. The derivative from the left is $+\infty$ exactly when a stronger condition holds, which also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of consecutive zeros among the digits $\xi_j$. For the value $-\infty$ the two sides are exchanged, and twos replace zeros. In particular, $T$ has an infinite derivative at every rational point that is not a ternary rational and whose period has different numbers of zeros and twos. For the finite cubes, we show that over every block of sizes $a3^k\le m\le(a+1)3^k$, the maximum of $\xi_n(m)$ exceeds the larger of its values at the two ends of the block by exactly $\max\{3^{k-|d|}-1,0\}$, where $d=n-k-s_3(a)$. Finally, the variation $V_n$ of $T$ over the partition of $[0,1]$ into the $3^n$ intervals $[m/3^n,(m+1)/3^n]$ satisfies $V_n/\sqrt n\to4/\sqrt{3\pi}$, and we compute the Fourier coefficients of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Chengyi Zhu

item.title: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics
item.description: arXiv:2610.21289v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A universal framework for Hopf algebras in combinatorics provides a unified understanding of combinatorial objects. To establish such a framework, we dualize the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras developed by Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile, obtaining the category of rooted Hopf algebras. An object in this category is a graded connected Hopf algebra equipped with a group-like element, called a root, in its completion. These roots dualize the character theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras and provide a natural way to extend Bernstein and raising operators to other rooted Hopf algebras. The resulting constructions extend Schur, Hall--Littlewood, and Macdonald functions to rooted Hopf algebras. As an application, we develop these constructions for symmetric functions in noncommuting variables.
item.dc:creator: Farid Aliniaeifard, Stephanie van Willigenburg

item.title: Matrix Completion Discriminants
item.description: arXiv:2610.21341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the matrix completion discriminant of a graph as the Zariski closure of the set of partial symmetric matrices whose completion fibers fail to meet a rank stratum transversely. A clique-sum formula for the matrix completion discriminant is established for arbitrary graphs, while explicit defining equations for cycles are obtained in terms of iterated resultants. Using these results together with the analysis of $K_4$-minor-free graphs, we prove that for every cycle-completable graph, the discriminant factors into determinant factors from maximal cliques and resultant factors from chordless cycles.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiyuki Sekiguchi, Shin-ichi Tanigawa

item.title: Optimally large cuts in both directions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every integer $d\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $m$, every digraph with $m$ edges and minimum outdegree at least $d$ has a vertex bipartition for which each directed cut is of size at least \[\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{2(2d-1)}m+\frac{d^2}{2(2d-1)}\right\rceil.\] The bound is sharp for infinitely many $m$. This answers for large graphs a question of Scott and proves a conjecture of Lee, Loh, and Sudakov. For $d=2$ we prove that $\lceil m/6\rceil$ is achievable for all $m$. We also establish a stability result characterizing near-extremal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Frederic Folz, Mykhaylo Tyomkyn

item.title: Stronger Spectral Bound for Clique Number
item.description: arXiv:2610.21388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an integer $k$, deciding whether a graph has a clique of size $k$ is an NP-complete problem. Wilf's inequality provides a spectral lower bound for the clique number of a graph. Strengthening this bound, Elphick and Wocjan proposed a conjecture in 2018 using positive adjacency eigenvalues. In this paper, we present an infinite family of graphs for which the Elphick and Wocjan conjecture is true. We find a stronger spectral lower bound for the clique number for this family of graphs.
item.dc:creator: Hareshkumar Jadav, Sudipta Mallik, Akhilesh Panchangam, Ranveer Singh

item.title: Ordinary lines, point degrees, and matroid density
item.description: arXiv:2610.21415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^d$ with full affine span, we prove that some point lies on at least $n+1-2n/(d+1)$ spanned lines, which is best possible in every dimension. By successive contraction, this implies the sharp bound $r+(\ell-3)\binom r2$ on the number of elements of a simple rank-$r$ complex-representable matroid excluding $U_{2,\ell}$ as a minor, which removes the sufficiently-large-rank assumption from the bound of Geelen, Nelson, and Walsh. An arithmetic application shows that rank-$r$ integer matrices whose maximal minors have absolute value at most $\Delta$ have at most $O(\Delta r^2)$ distinct columns, resolving a question of Averkov and Schymura. We prove that a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}^3$ determines at least $n^2/40$ ordinary lines whenever no plane contains more than $2n/3$ of the points. This answers a question of Basit, Dvir, Saraf, and Wolf. We also prove upper bounds on average line length and lower bounds on the number of points incident to many spanned lines in high-dimensional point sets. The proofs combine contraction of concentrated flats with normalization of the point vectors and second- and fourth-moment estimates on their pairwise correlations. This approach builds on the design matrix method.
item.dc:creator: Matthew E. Kroeker, Ben Lund

item.title: Curvature-Distortion Numbers of Graphs: Prescribed Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.21454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an optimization problem for weighted Lin--Lu--Yau curvature. Given a graph $G=(V,E)$ and a prescribed lower curvature bound $k\ge0$, we ask for the smallest multiplicative distortion \[ \Dist(w):=\frac{\sup_{e\in E}w_e}{\inf_{e\in E}w_e} \] of the edge weights needed to make every edge have curvature at least $k$. This leads to the family \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G) := \inf\bigl\{ \Dist(w): \kappa_{\LLY}^{w}(e)\ge k \text{ for every }e\in E(G) \bigr\}, \] which extends the nonnegative-curvature invariant introduced in our preceding paper \cite{Xia2026InvariantI}. The edge weights change the transition probabilities, while the combinatorial graph distance remains fixed. Positive prescribed curvature leads to a fundamental distinction from the case $k=0$. If $G$ is a connected locally finite infinite graph and $k>0$, then \[ \DN_{\LLY}^{k}(G)=\infty. \] Thus no finite multiplicative distortion of the edge weights can impose a uniform positive curvature lower bound on such a graph. For a finite tree $T$ with $m$ edges, such weights exist exactly when $k\le2/m$. We prove that the minimum distortion is attained by a weight unique up to scaling, and that the normalized minimizer and its distortion depend continuously and nondecreasingly on $k$. We then extend the finite-tree theory to general connected graphs. As an application, we characterize the graphs of girth at least six for which finite $k$-distortion is possible.
item.dc:creator: Qing Xia

item.title: Ehrhart positivity for paving positroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central conjecture of Ferroni, Jochemko, and Schr\"{o}ter posits that every positroid is Ehrhart positive. While Ehrhart positivity has recently been verified for notable classes such as lattice path matroids and series-parallel matroids, the general conjecture remains open. In this paper, we prove that the base polytope of any paving positroid has positive Ehrhart coefficients. This establishes a new class of Ehrhart positive positroids and provides substantial evidence supporting this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Strong coloring numbers of grids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive integers $n$ and $d$, the $d$-dimensional grid of side length $n$ is the graph $G(n,d)$ with vertex set $[n]^d$, in which two vertices are adjacent if they differ by $1$ in exactly one coordinate and agree in all the other coordinates. We determine, for every fixed $d$, the asymptotic growth in $r$ of the $r$th strong coloring numbers of these grids. More precisely for $n$ large enough, ${\rm scol}_r(G(n,d)) = \Omega_d\bigl(r^{d-1}\bigr)$ as $r\to\infty$. This matches an upper bound given by a volume packing argument, which holds more generally for touching graphs of unit balls in $\mathbb R^d$. For the lower bound, we construct in $G(n,d)$ a bramble of order $\Omega_d(n^{d-1})$ with each element of radius at most $dn$. This construction was found by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Micek, Torsten Ueckerdt

item.title: Rectangular Symmetry for Catalan Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Katabolizable tableaux provide a combinatorial formula for the Schur coefficients of Catalan functions. We prove that a tableau involution preserves katabolizability under antidiagonal reflection of any upper root ideal. This involution complements shape and content in a fixed rectangle and preserves charge. We obtain a bijective proof of the rectangular symmetry of these coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Hyeonjae Choi

item.title: Lattice coverings by parallelotopes containing cube vertices
item.description: arXiv:2610.21572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate when a parallelotope containing vertices of the unit cube $Q_n=[0,1]^n$ covers $\Bbb R^n$ by integer translates. We prove the covering property for every parallelepiped containing five vertices of $Q_3$, and, in any dimension, for every parallelotope containing a facet of $Q_n$ and one vertex of the opposite facet. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp bound $1/n$ for the volume of a pyramid contained in $Q_n$ with a parallelotope base. We also give an alternative proof of this bound.
item.dc:creator: Dragomir Grozev, Nikolai Nikolov

item.title: Generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
item.description: arXiv:2610.21577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with exponent $\exp(G)$. For positive integer $k$, the generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant, denoted by $\mathsf s_{k\exp(G)}(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of length at least $\ell$ over $G$ has a zero-sum subsequence of length $k\exp(G)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any $n\ge 1$, \[\mathsf s_{3\cdot 2^n}(C_{2^n}^3)=6\cdot 2^n-3 \quad\text{and}\quad \mathsf s_{4\cdot 3^n}(C_{3^n}^3)=7\cdot 3^n-3. \] This completes all the remaining cases in the study of $\mathsf s_{kq}(C_q^3)$, where $q$ is a prime power and $k\ge 3$. As a consequence, for every $k\ge 3$, we have \[ \mathsf s_{kn}(C_n^3)=(k+3)n+O(\frac{n}{\log n}). \] This verifies a conjecture of Kubertin asymptotically. Our approach combines the previous group ring techniques and a recent powerful generalization of the Chevalley-Warning and Ax-Katz theorems introduced by Grynkiewicz
item.dc:creator: Hanbin Zhang, Shiwen Zhang

item.title: An Eventown Result for Multisets
item.description: arXiv:2610.21636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an extension of the Eventown problem of sets to multisets on $[n] = \{1,2,...,n\}$. A multiset is called $m$-bounded if each element has multiplicity at most $m$. The intersection of two multisets is defined as the multiset in which each element has multiplicity equal to the minimum of its multiplicities in the two original multisets. A family of $m$-bounded multisets is called an Eventown family if every member and the intersection of every pair of distinct members has even cardinality, with cardinalities counted with multiplicities. We determine the maximum size $E_m(n)$ of such a family for every $m$ and $n$. We show that $ E_{2q}(n)=(q+1)^n, $ and $ E_{2q+1}(n)=(q+1)^{n-2k}\bigl((q+1)^2+1\bigr)^k,$ where $k=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. In particular, the case $m=1$ recovers the classical Eventown theorem for sets. We also characterize all extremal families for $m\ge2$. For even $m$, the unique extremal family consists of all multisets in which every element has even multiplicity. For odd $m\ge3$, every extremal family has a product structure arising from two explicit families on pairs of coordinates, together with an additional coordinate restricted to even multiplicities when $n$ is odd. Consequently, there are exactly $k+1$ extremal types up to permutations of the ground set.
item.dc:creator: Anirban Banerjee, Abisek Dewan

item.title: A simple classification of the special matchings in the symmetric group
item.description: arXiv:2610.21647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a simple characterization of special matchings of all Bruhat intervals in the symmetric group, yielding an explicit classification that depends only on the one-line notations of the endpoints. We also study extensions of graded posets by partial special matchings, proving the existence and uniqueness of such extensions and providing an explicit construction. Combining these results, we obtain a combinatorial algorithm for computing Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials for an isomorphism-closed family of Bruhat intervals that includes all intervals whose bottom element has length at most one.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Caselli, Mario Marietti

item.title: Graphs with three eigenvalues from group divisible designs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct biregular graphs with three distinct eigenvalues from semiregular group divisible designs. For every prime power $q$, we use the spectral structure of Muzychuk's Construction~A on $q+1$ copies of $\operatorname{AG}(2,q^2)$ to produce suitable group divisible designs. The resulting biregular graphs have $2q^5+q^4+q^2$ vertices and distinct eigenvalues $q^5+q^3+q^2$, $q^2$, and $-q^2$. Their coherent closures have rank $12$ and type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&5\end{smallmatrix}\right]$. We also determine the four-class symmetric association schemes that are the coherent closures of the auxiliary graphs in this family. Computational searches provide further graphs on $81$ and $156$ vertices, using Muzychuk's Construction~B and a generalised quadrangle, respectively; their coherent closures have ranks $13$ and $10$. The $156$-vertex example has a strongly regular design as its coherent closure, of type $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}3&2\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right]$, answering a question of the authors. We also realise a $126$-vertex example by switching a strongly regular graph.
item.dc:creator: Gary Greaves, Jose Yip

item.title: Orlik-Solomon algebras determine the Tutte polynomials of matroids of rank at most three
item.description: arXiv:2610.21812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a simple matroid of rank $r$ on the ground set $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ denote its Tutte polynomial, and let $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ denote its Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. We say that $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})$ determines $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)$ if, for every simple matroid $\mathcal{N}$, an isomorphism $\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{M})\cong\mathrm{OS}(\mathcal{N})$ of $\mathbb{C}$-algebras, without regard to the grading, implies $T_{\mathcal{M}}(x,y)=T_{\mathcal{N}}(x,y)$. Falk conjectured that the Orlik-Solomon $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of every simple matroid of rank three determines its Tutte polynomial. We prove that this holds for every simple matroid of rank at most three, thereby resolving Falk's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Jianxuan Luo, Tingzeng Wu, Hong-Jian Lai

item.title: Rich-neighbor 5-edge-colorings of subcubic graphs whose 3-vertices induce a matching
item.description: arXiv:2610.21868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\varphi$ be a proper edge-coloring of a graph $G$. An edge is called rich if all edges adjacent to it receive pairwise distinct colors. The coloring $\varphi$ is a rich-neighbor edge-coloring if every non-isolated edge is adjacent to a rich edge. Petru\v{s}evski and \v{S}krekovski introduced this notion as a relaxation of strong edge-coloring and conjectured that every connected subcubic graph other than $K_4$ admits a rich-neighbor $5$-edge-coloring. We establish the conjectured bound for every subcubic graph $G$ satisfying $\Delta(G[V_3])\leq 1,$ where $V_3$ is the set of vertices of degree $3$ in $G$. Equivalently, the $3$-vertices of $G$ induce a matching together with isolated vertices. This extends the result of Chen, Tan and Zhou for subcubic graphs with no adjacent $3$-vertices.
item.dc:creator: Jiangxu Kong, Zhuming Lin, Yan Wang

item.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Delta_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\Delta_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.
item.dc:creator: Hai Zhu

item.title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.21921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^{\nu}_{\lambda,\mu}=3$, then $c^{M\nu}_{M\lambda,M\mu}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{\lambda,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $\beta=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $\sigma$, we show that if $\beta$ is $\sigma$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $\sigma$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $\sigma$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.
item.dc:creator: Deepanshu Prasad

item.title: Cayley graphs of abelian groups, circular colorings and discrete fundamental groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.21940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each integer $k \ge 2$, we prove that an abelian group $\Gamma$ satisfies $\exp(\Gamma) \in \{1,\dots,k\} \cup \{2,4,\dots,2k\}$ if and only if it admits no non-bipartite Cayley graph whose circular chromatic number is strictly less than $2 + \frac{2}{k-1}$. This refines the algebraic characterization by Krebs and Sankar of abelian groups that admit $3$-chromatic Cayley graphs.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Enami, Takahiro Matsushita

item.title: A complete classification of perfect state transfer in Grover walks on abelian Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.21946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely classify connected Cayley graphs over finite abelian groups that exhibit perfect state transfer in Grover walks. First, we show that a Cayley graph over any finite group exhibiting perfect state transfer has valency $1$, $2$, or $4$. For valency $4$, we prove that an abelian Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if $S=\{a,-a,a+h,-a+h\}$, where $h$ has order $2$, and $4\nmid |\Gamma|/2$. Combining this characterization with the valency-one and valency-two cases, we explicitly determine all pairs $(\Gamma,S)$ for which $\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ exhibits perfect state transfer. Our results extend the classification of circulant graphs of valency at most four obtained by Kubota and Yoshino [Circulant graphs with valency up to 4 that admit perfect state transfer in Grover walks, \emph{J. Comb. Theory Ser. A.}, 216 (2025) 106064] to Cayley graphs over arbitrary finite abelian groups and to all valencies.
item.dc:creator: Koushik Bhakta, Bikash Bhattacharjya

item.title: The asymptotic Erd{\H{o}}s--Frankl--F\"uredi cover-free conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.22021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1985, Erd{\H{o}}s, Frankl and F{\"u}redi conjectured that the threshold $T(r)$ for the existence of an $r$-cover-free family with more members than points satisfies $T(r)=(1+o(1))r^2$. We confirm this conjecture by proving $T(r)\ge r^2+r+2$ for every $r\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Xinqi Huang, Hong Liu

item.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.
item.dc:creator: Hirotake Kurihara

item.title: Integral homology lattices of matching and circulant complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bouc's hook cycles span the rational top homology of the matching complex of $K_{2k+1}$. We prove that their integral saturation quotient has exponent exactly $2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$ for every $k\geq1$, and construct divided-power cycles attaining this bound. For $k\geq2$, the homology lattice is not isomorphic to the standard integral hook lattice as an $\mathfrak S_{2k+1}$-module. For circulant complexes, we determine the integral dihedral homology modules of $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s}^{s-1})$, $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+1}^{s-1})$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(C_{3s+2}^{s-1})$, for $s\geq3$, $s\geq2$ and $s\geq3$, respectively, and classify the least scalar lifts of all primitive equivariant quotients to the rank-one module with trivial rotation and negative reflection. Tate localization relates prime-order gluing to fixed-point homology under a free, single-degree homology hypothesis. Explicit cycle subgroups separate saturation defects from obstructions to equivariant sections. For circulant independence complexes with jumps two and three, we prove an eight-periodic ordinary homotopy classification and a fixed-space obstruction to uniform representation suspensions. For every fixed nonempty bounded positive jump set, a finite-state construction gives a rational critical-face series.
item.dc:creator: Qihang Wang, Weiye Li

item.title: Barrier Log-Concavity of Large Forests
item.description: arXiv:2610.22098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the independence sequence of every sufficiently large forest is strictly barrier log-concave: whenever $i_{k+1}>i_k$, one has $i_k^2>i_{k-1}i_{k+1}$. Consequently, every common downward coefficient tilt is unimodal, with one order threshold valid simultaneously for all $0<t\le1$. As an application, we prove that every sufficiently large well-covered tree has a strictly log-concave independence polynomial. More generally, the latter conclusion holds for well-covered forests with sufficiently large matching number. Every sufficiently large forest with a palindromic independence polynomial is also strictly log-concave, with its modes at the central ranks. The proof establishes local coefficient-curvature estimates uniformly over forests of unbounded maximum degree and over activities tending to zero. Combined with the fixed-density theorem of Fang, Lu, Nevo, Yao, and Zheng, these estimates complete the strict log-concavity interval down to rank one through $\lfloor17\alpha/25\rfloor$; the terminal fraction is inherited. The classical decreasing tail then yields the barrier property. A cumulative-coefficient corona theorem transfers barrier log-concavity of the base forest to full strict log-concavity of its leaf corona.
item.dc:creator: Vadim E. Levit

item.title: Unavoidable flats in GF(q)-representable matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.22135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that, for any finite field $\mathbb{F}$ and positive integer $k$, a simple $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid $M$ with sufficiently high rank contains a rank-$k$ flat which is either independent in $M$, or is a projective or affine geometry over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}$. This generalizes a result for matroids representable over prime fields due to the first two authors. As a corollary, we obtain a Ramsey theorem for matroids representable over a finite field $\mathbb{F}$. For an integer $k$, in any $2$-colouring of the points of an $\mathbb{F}$-representable matroid of sufficiently high rank, there is a monochromatic rank-$k$ flat.
item.dc:creator: Jim Geelen, Matthew E. Kroeker, Peter Nelson

item.title: Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an edge-colored graph, the wild number measures how close the graph is to having a spanning tree in every color. We investigate this parameter for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, with particular emphasis on minimum proper colorings and equitable $2$-colorings. For complete graphs, we determine the full range of wild numbers attainable by equitable $2$-colorings and show that, although every value in this range occurs, the expected wild number of a uniformly random equitable $2$-coloring tends to $0$ as the order of the graph grows. For minimum proper colorings of $K_n$, we establish a general lower bound, determine the exact wild number for $3 \le n \le 12$, and conjecture that the lower bound is sharp for all $n$. We also develop structural conditions on ideal wild sets and use them to obtain upper bounds and analyze the performance of a natural greedy algorithm. For complete bipartite graphs, we prove a sharp upper bound for equitable $2$-colorings and determine the wild number exactly for minimum proper colorings. Finally, we apply these results to Cartesian products of complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, obtaining lower bounds for the wild number under minimum proper and product colorings.
item.dc:creator: Aleyah Dawkins, Alexander Nappo, Jessie Tong, Christopher Zimbizi

item.title: Logical isomorphism and logical limit laws for small permutation classes and regular languages
item.description: arXiv:2610.22218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we show that for each small permutation class $\mathcal{F}$ there exists a regular language $L_\mathcal{F}$ such that the monadic second-order TOTO logic on $\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to classical monadic second-order logic on $L_\mathcal{F}$. Thanks to the fact that regular languages are closed under monadic second-order restrictions this shows that many subsets of $\mathcal{F}$ have a well-behaved structure. In particular, this allows us to show that random permutations from any small permutation class satisfies convergence laws for both first-order logic and monadic second-order logic. In the latter case, the law is modular. Our proofs introduce a way of using the automaton description of regular languages to prove properties of generating functions which may be of independent interest. Potential applications include first-order limit laws for random words in some regular languages.
item.dc:creator: Klas Marstr\"om, Eero R\"aty

item.title: Uniform Intersection Numbers and Subgroup-Based Generating Graphs of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The uniform intersection number of a finite group $G$, denoted by $ui(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that the intersection of any $k$ distinct maximal subgroups of $G$ is equal to its Frattini subgroup. We determine the uniform intersection number of dicyclic, dihedral, and quasi-dihedral groups. We then investigate the uniform intersection number through the subgroup-based generating graph $\mathcal{G}(G)$ of a finite group $G$. We characterize the finite groups $G$ for which both the intersection number and the uniform intersection number are equal to two, and show that this condition is equivalent to $\mathcal{G}(G)$ being complete multipartite. We also classify finite groups in terms of the diameter, girth, and perfectness of $\mathcal{G}(G)$. Finally, we show that $\mathcal{G}(\mathbb{Z}_n)$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $n=p_1^{r}p_2^{r}$, where $r\geq 2$ and $p_1$ and $p_2$ are distinct primes.
item.dc:creator: Projesh Nath Choudhury, Biswaranjan Khanra

item.title: An Induced Subgraph Paradigm for Strongly Regular Graph Constructions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How many disjoint copies of some graph $H$ can appear in an induced subgraph of a strongly regular graph? We give upper and lower bounds that depend on the number of vertices in their boundary. This generalizes a result of Lou-Murin which bounds the independence number of a (hitherto still elusive) strongly regular graph with parameters $(99,14,1,2)$. The equality cases suggest alternative structural approaches for potential constructions of such a graph. We show, using computer searches, that one cannot impose certain additional natural conditions for some of the cases.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Baker

item.title: A polylogarithmic bound for list replicability
item.description: arXiv:2610.20657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zhang [Zha26] recently posted a manuscript announcing that the list-replicability number of every class of $M\ge 2$ binary concepts on $N\ge 2$ domain points is $O(\log^2 M\log N)$, which would be the first polylogarithmic upper bound on this quantity. In this note, we present a short, self-contained proof of this bound, following the high-level approach of the manuscript but with considerably simpler arguments.
item.dc:creator: Ari Blondal, Hamed Hatami, Pooya Hatami, Chavdar Lalov, Sivan Tretiak

item.title: Crystallization of the undertile
item.description: arXiv:2610.20663v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify all periodic tilings with a monotile known as $\mathbf{R1}$ and called here the undertile, which underlies several aperiodic monotiles such as the Taylor-Socolar one. The classification is done using deflation, through a study of fracture lines between zones where deflation can be performed. A full classification of fracture patterns is given, that also applies to non-periodic tilings with the undertile. This can be used to reprove non-periodicity of some existing monotiles based on the undertile.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Ch\'eritat

item.title: Eccentricity Shortest Path: the structural parameter landscape
item.description: arXiv:2610.20769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Eccentricity Shortest Path problem asks, given a connected graph and a nonnegative integer $R$, whether some shortest path is within distance $R$ of every vertex. We study its structural parameterized complexity. We give fixed-parameter algorithms for vertex-deletion distance to cographs, vertex-deletion distance to interval graphs, and bandwidth. The interval-deletion result answers a question of Bhyravarapu et al. (IWOCA 2023). We obtain XP algorithms for vertex-deletion distance to chordal graphs, clique-width, and rank-width, without requiring expressions or decompositions for the latter two. Consequently, the problem is polynomial-time solvable for every fixed treewidth, answering a question of Chakraborty et al. (2026). We also derive fixed-parameter tractability for treedepth and XP membership for diameter from earlier algorithms. We prove $\mathsf{W}[3]$-hardness for cutwidth, and hence pathwidth and treewidth, even on graphs of maximum degree at most five; $\mathsf{W}[2]$-hardness for vertex clique-cover number; and NP-hardness on graphs of tree-independence number at most two. For maximum leaf number $\ell$, we obtain an $O(\ell^4)$-bit compression and a polynomial kernel. Finally, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{coNP}/\mathrm{poly}$, we exclude polynomial kernels for bandwidth, feedback edge number, vertex-deletion distance to a clique, and vertex cover number. The last bound also excludes polynomial kernels for vertex-deletion distance to proper interval graphs.
item.dc:creator: Anand Babu, Ashwin Jacob, Hitendra Kumar, R. B. Sandeep

item.title: The Lov\'asz number is not alone: a continuum of R\'enyi points in the entanglement-assisted spectrum of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.20775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Li and Zuiddam's entanglement-assisted asymptotic spectrum of graphs consists of the normalized graph parameters that are additive under disjoint unions, multiplicative under strong products and monotone under entanglement-assisted cohomomorphisms; the entanglement-assisted Shannon capacity is their pointwise minimum. To our knowledge, the Lov\'asz number $\vartheta$ was its only known element. We find a continuum of others. Three quantities of Duan and Winter, $\log_2\vartheta$, the minimal Holevo capacity $C_{\min}$ and the logarithm of the no-signalling simulation cost $\Sigma$, are the smallest information radii of classical-quantum channels compatible with a graph, measured with Petz-R\'enyi divergences of orders $0$, $1$ and $2$. At order zero this is due to Schrijver (as credited by Dalai) and to Duan and Winter; at order one it is the min-max formula for the Holevo capacity. Interpolating in the order gives a family $\vartheta_\alpha$, $0\le\alpha\le2$, and we prove that every member lies in the spectrum. The main step, multiplicativity under strong products for channels that need not factor, follows from an exact nesting identity for compressions. Sandwiched R\'enyi radii of order $\beta\in[1/2,\infty]$ give the same family, at $\alpha=2-1/\beta$. On the five-cycle the family takes every value in $[\sqrt5,5/2]$. A Hilbert-Schmidt inequality for the pentagon gives $C_{\min}(C_5)=\log_2(5/2)$, proving a conjecture of Duan and Winter. We also settle the two open links of their inequality chain: the graph-level no-signalling simulation rate always equals its single-letter value $\log_2\Sigma(G)$, and a 32-vertex graph from the Mermin-Peres magic square has $C_{\min}<\log_2\Sigma$, certified in exact rational arithmetic. Finally, $\Sigma$ never exceeds the projective rank of the complement; a rank inequality for the same square makes this strict on a 1440-vertex graph.
item.dc:creator: Nidhal Mghirbi, Seth Douglas

item.title: Two Short Proofs of the $A^A$ Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.20802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1984, D.~Duffus asked whether $A^A\cong B^B$ implies $A\cong B$ for finite, nonempty ordered sets $A$ and~$B$. J.\,D. Farley and the author proved that it does. In this paper, we give two short proofs using all intervals of maximum height and the elements with exactly one lower cover. The first proof averages over these intervals; the second takes their disjoint sum and constructs three invariants. Both avoid the auxiliary ordering, direct factorization, and canonical coordinates of the earlier proof.
item.dc:creator: George Gr\"atze

item.title: Perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware
item.description: arXiv:2610.20855v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We run continuous-time quantum walks with perfect and peak state transfer on a present-day superconducting quantum processor, IBM Quantum's $156$-qubit Heron device ibm_kingston, deliberately without error correction or error mitigation. Perfect state transfer and its relaxations have been studied extensively in algebraic graph theory, where one can prove exactly which graphs move a quantum state from one vertex to another with probability one (or with the largest probability the graph allows, in the case of peak state transfer), and at what time. Our experiments cover perfect state transfer on the hypercubes $Q_2 = C_4$ and $Q_3$, and on the Hamming-weighted paths $\mathrm{HP}_n$, the equitable-partition quotients of the hypercubes $Q_n$, for $n$ up to $20$; peak state transfer on the $X_n$ family for $n$ up to $11$; and, for comparison, moving the state along a path of qubits by a sequence of SWAP gates.
item.dc:creator: Priscilla Awuah, Krystal Guo

item.title: Ehrhart Polynomials of Triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.20899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present two ways of constructing Ehrhart polynomials corresponding to certain triangles in $\mathbb{R}^3$. One of our methods employs Popoviciu's Theorem, while the other method uses a version of Pick's Theorem adapted to rank-2 lattices in $\mathbb{R}^3$. We then apply our methods to linear Diophantine equations of the form $ax+by+cz=n$ and develop upper and lower bounds on the number of solutions in nonnegative integers $x$, $y$, and $z$. The bounds we develop are closed form quasi-polynomials, and the difference between them is bounded by a constant depending only on $a$ and $b$. As an application, we prove that the $k$th Frobenius number exists for any triple of positive integers and any $k$.
item.dc:creator: Max Aldrich, Daniel Gulbrandsen, Clara Keddy

item.title: Beyond 11/16: dense Kuramoto networks that resist synchrony
item.description: arXiv:2610.21271v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How densely must a network of identical Kuramoto oscillators be wired before synchrony is its only stable state? The answer is a critical connectivity $\mu_c$ (the minimum degree divided by $n-1$), known to satisfy $11/16\le\mu_c<3/4$. We raise the lower bound from $11/16=0.6875$ to $\mu_c\ge(4+2q^*)/(7+q^*)=0.6929077\ldots$, where $q^*\approx0.6506$ is a root of an explicit polynomial of degree 8. The networks approaching this bound carry stable states that hug the four-cluster state: three neighboring clusters each split into two slightly separated halves, and the four crossed links between neighboring halves (those whose phase gap deviates most from a quarter turn) have densities approaching $q^*$. We build these networks from a coarse-grained cluster model, verify stability with interval arithmetic, and blow the model up into large networks with an exact minimum degree. The states are fragile and easily missed by numerical searches that impose stability margins.
item.dc:creator: Kevin P. O'Keeffe

item.title: Star-Ordered Rotor Loops in Clifford Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.21593v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider, in a real Clifford algebra, a family of unit bivectors $B_i = C S_i$ formed from $k+1$ pairwise anticommuting generators $C, S_1, \ldots, S_k$ with square $-1$; we call this a \emph{star family} with \emph{central generator} $C$ and \emph{leaf generators} $S_i$. For the associated rotors $U_i(\theta_i) = \cos\frac{\theta_i}{2} + B_i \sin\frac{\theta_i}{2}$ we study two objects: the ordered chain $P_k = U_1 \cdots U_k$ and the \emph{star-ordered rotor loop} $\Theta_k = P_k \, Q_k$ with the \emph{same-order reversion product} $Q_k = \widetilde U_1 \cdots \widetilde U_k$, as opposed to the trivially reversed order, for which $U_1 \cdots U_k \widetilde U_k \cdots \widetilde U_1 = 1$. The scalar part of $\Theta_k$ measures the \emph{order defect} of the family. We prove two theorems. First, the scalar part of the chain factorises, $\langle P_k \rangle_0 = \prod_{i=1}^k \cos\frac{\theta_i}{2}$; this requires the star structure, and we give a counterexample. Second, we derive a closed expression for $\langle \Theta_k \rangle_0$, valid for every $k$, whose coefficients obey a \emph{period-four sign law} $\eta(m) = (-1)^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor}$ and which admits the compact form $\langle \Theta_k \rangle_0 = \operatorname{Re}\!\big[(1-\mathrm{i}) \prod_i (\cos^2\frac{\theta_i}{2} + \mathrm{i}\sin^2\frac{\theta_i}{2})\big]$, holding for every pairwise anticommuting unit family without further hypothesis. From the compact form we obtain a polar form, a complete zero criterion, a lacunary coefficient rule, and a proof of non-separability for $k \geq 2$. Two supplementary theorems extend the result to arbitrary permutations of the index order and to families with mixed squares $B_i^2 \in \{-1, +1\}$. All proofs use only anticommutation, reversion and the symmetry of the scalar form; no physical interpretation is assumed or claimed.
item.dc:creator: Nik Jenzer

item.title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_\delta$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_\delta$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.
item.dc:creator: Mingze Li

item.title: Edge ideals of gapfree graphs with matching number $3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21866v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that if $G$ is a gapfree graph with matching number $3$, then every power $I(G)^q$, $q\geq2$, of its edge ideal has linear quotients, and hence a linear resolution. Our approach combines graph reductions based on clique domination of gapfree graphs and matching number with operations preserving linear quotients. We reduce the problem to $26$ non-co-chordal graphs on at most seven vertices. A new preservation theorem for gapfree edge addition, together with known results on duplication and gapfree expansion, handles all but one of these graphs. For the remaining graph on seven vertices, we construct a linear quotients ordering for the square and extend it recursively to every higher power.
item.dc:creator: Nursel Erey, T\`ai Huy H\`a, Takayuki Hibi, Selvi Kara, Susan Morey

item.title: On the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences arising from nilpotent actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22076v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every polynomial multicorrelation sequence arising from nilpotent actions admits a decomposition into a generalized nilsequence and a null-sequence. This resolves a long-standing question of Frantzikinakis concerning the structure of polynomial multicorrelation sequences of commuting transformations. Our proof builds upon ideas underlying the norm convergence theorem of Walsh.
item.dc:creator: Jovan Andreevski, Felipe Hern\'andez

item.title: A quadratic ancestor inequality for spanning trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.22180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a quadratic ancestor inequality for weighted spanning trees on finite undirected graphs and give two applications. First, for every finite $n$-vertex transitive graph, the expected distance in its uniform spanning tree (UST) between two independent uniform vertices is at least $\sqrt{n}-1$, resolving a conjecture in [Benjamini--Kozma, Comm. Math. Phys. 259 (2005), 257--286]. Second, we prove that the growth exponent of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) is at least 3/2.
item.dc:creator: Gefei Cai

item.title: Connectivity Bounds for GHZ Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states are multipartite entangled quantum states that play a central role in quantum information theory, with applications in quantum communication, cryptography, and distributed quantum computing. A major experimental goal is to create high-dimensional GHZ states using multiple entangled parties. Krenn, Gu and Zeilinger discovered a surprising bridge between these quantum-optical experiments and graph theory: certain photonic experiments can be represented by edge-coloured, edge-weighted graphs, and the dimension of the produced GHZ state equals the number of feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings. This led Krenn and Gu to conjecture that every GHZ graph with more than four vertices has dimension at most $2$. A counterexample would give a new high-dimensional multipartite GHZ construction, while a proof would clarify fundamental resource limitations in quantum optics. It is known that the conjecture holds for graphs of vertex connectivity at most $2$ [MFCS 2024], and that simple GHZ graphs with $n>4$ vertices have dimension less than $n/\sqrt{2}$ [Quantum 2024]. However, no general upper bound depending only on vertex connectivity was known. We prove that every simple connected GHZ graph $G$ with at least four vertices has dimension at most $2^{\kappa(G)-1}+\binom{\kappa(G)}{2}$, where $\kappa(G)$ is the vertex connectivity of $G$. We also prove new bounds in terms of edge connectivity and maximum degree.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala

item.title: Geometric Graph Representations via Compact SAT Encodings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present compact SAT encodings and certifying exact solvers for boxicity and cubicity. The boxicity of a graph is the minimum dimension in which it is the intersection graph of axis-aligned boxes; cubicity is defined analogously using unit cubes. Grid-based formulations face a geometric discretization bottleneck, growing rapidly with the target dimension. We avoid this bottleneck by encoding the total order of interval endpoints in each coordinate. For an $n$-vertex graph and target dimension $d$, our boxicity encoding uses $O(n^2d)$ variables and $O(n^3d)$ clauses, both linear in $d$. Requiring the left- and right-endpoint orders to agree yields a cubicity encoding of the same asymptotic size. Satisfying models are decoded into independently checked geometric representations, while unsatisfiable instances used as lower-bound evidence carry mechanically verified DRAT certificates. In a controlled evaluation with 186 trials per encoding on standard and structured graph families, the order encoding solves 96.8% of trials, compared with 71.0% for the known grid formulation, and reduces mean PAR-2 time from 178.21 to 21.70 seconds. The pipeline also certifies exact values for several named graphs. We turn one such value into a reusable obstruction by proving that every Kneser graph $K(n,k)$ with $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$ contains an induced Desargues graph. The resulting lower bound, together with an explicit three-dimensional representation of $K(7,3)$, establishes $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(7,3))=3$. This disproves the conjecture of Caoduro and Sebo that $\operatorname{boxicity}(K(n,k))=n-k$ for all $k\ge3$ and $n\ge2k+1$.
item.dc:creator: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala, Suraj Kumar Sahoo, Aatman Supkar

item.title: Tensor-generating line bundles on toric varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A line bundle is $\otimes$-generating if its powers generate the derived category of perfect complexes. Refining the derived Nakai--Moishezon criterion of Ito--Olander, we characterize $\otimes$-generating line bundles on proper toric varieties by a combinatorial criterion on the fan, leading to the notion of $\otimes$-generating fans characterizing $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Furthermore, we prove an analogue of Kleiman's criterion of ampleness for $\otimes$-generation. As applications, we provide several examples including: (i) smooth proper fourfolds with no $\otimes$-generating line bundle, by showing that products of two or more positive-dimensional proper toric varieties admit a $\otimes$-generating line bundle only when they are projective, (ii) families of smooth non-projective proper threefolds with $\otimes$-generating canonical bundles. Finally, we study subvarieties obstructing $\otimes$-generation of canonical bundles and implications to autoequivalences of derived categories.
item.dc:creator: Daigo Ito, Michael R. Zeng, Xiangru Zeng

item.title: New scattered linearized quadrinomials
item.description: arXiv:2402.14742v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1<t<n$ be integers, where $t$ is a divisor of $n$. An R-$q^t$-partially scattered polynomial is a $\mathbb F_q$-linearized polynomial $f$ in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ that satisfies the condition that for all $x,y\in\mathbb F_{q^n}^*$ such that $x/y\in\mathbb F_{q^t}$, if $f(x)/x=f(y)/y$, then $x/y\in\mathbb F_q$; $f$ is called scattered if this implication holds for all $x,y\in\mathbb F_{q^n}^*$. Two polynomials in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ are said to be equivalent if their graphs are in the same orbit under the action of the group $\Gamma L(2,q^n)$. For $n>8$ only three families of scattered polynomials in $\mathbb F_{q^n}[X]$ are known: $(i)$~monomials of pseudoregulus type, $(ii)$~binomials of Lunardon-Polverino type, and $(iii)$~a family of quadrinomials defined in [1,10] and extended in [8,13]. In this paper we prove that the polynomial $\varphi_{m,q^J}=X^{q^{J(t-1)}}+X^{q^{J(2t-1)}}+m(X^{q^J}-X^{q^{J(t+1)}})\in\mathbb F_{q^{2t}}[X]$, $q$ odd, $t\ge3$ is R-$q^t$-partially scattered for every value of $m\in\mathbb F_{q^t}^*$ and $J$ coprime with $2t$. Moreover, for every $t>4$ and $q>5$ there exist values of $m$ for which $\varphi_{m,q}$ is scattered and new with respect to the polynomials mentioned in $(i)$, $(ii)$ and $(iii)$ above. The related linear sets are of $\Gamma L$-class at least two.
item.dc:creator: Valentino Smaldore, Corrado Zanella, Ferdinando Zullo

item.title: Completely regular codes in graphs covered by a Hamming graph
item.description: arXiv:2411.09698v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Cayley graphs on the additive group of a small vector space over GF$(q)$, $q=2,3$, we look for completely regular (CR) codes whose parameters are new in Hamming graphs over the same field. The existence of a CR code in such a Cayley graph $G$ implies the existence of a CR code with the same parameters in the corresponding Hamming graph that covers $G$. In such a way, we find several completely regular codes with new parameters in Hamming graphs over GF(2) and GF(3). The most interesting findings are two new CR-1 (with covering radius 1) codes that are independent sets (such CR are equivalent to optimal orthogonal arrays attaining the Bierbrauer-Friedman bound) and one new CR-2 code. By recursive constructions, every new CR code induces an infinite sequence of CR codes (in particular, optimal orthogonal arrays if the original code is CR-1 and independent). Some of the found ternary CR codes disprove a conjectured generalization of the correlation-immunity bound on the strength of binary orthogonal arrays to the non-binary case. In between, we classify feasible parameters of CR codes in several strongly regular graphs. Keywords: completely regular codes, Hamming graphs, Cayley graphs, strongly regular graphs, graph covering, orthogonal arrays
item.dc:creator: Sergey Goryainov, Denis Krotov

item.title: Mixing and Merging Metric Spaces using Directed Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2505.06405v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X_1,d_1),\dots,(X_N,d_N)$ be metric spaces with $d_i:X_i\times X_i\to[0,1]$ and let $X=\prod_{i=1}^N X_i$. Let $G$ be a directed graph with vertex set $[N]=\{1,\dots,N\}$ and edge set $E(G)$. Given edge weights $P=\{p_{ij}\in(0,1]:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$, define the closed in-neighborhood $B_j(G):=\{j\}\cup\{i:(i,j)\in E(G)\}$ and put $p_{jj}=1$. Define, for $g,h\in X$, \[ d_{X,G,P}(g,h)\;:=\;1-\frac{1}{N}\sum_{j=1}^N\ \prod_{i\in B_j(G)}\bigl(1-d_i(g_i,h_i)\bigr)^{1/p_{ij}}. \] We prove that $d_{X,G,P}$ is a metric and analyze its behavior under graph operations (disjoint unions, Cartesian products). Two quantitative principles govern this family: (i) \emph{edge densification} (adding edges) increases the distance pointwise and in expectation, with an exact single-edge increment formula and a uniform $1/N$ sensitivity bound; and (ii) \emph{weight monotonicity}: increasing an edge weight $p_{ij}$ decreases the metric. When the coordinate pairs are independent across coordinates, we obtain a closed-form factorization of the mean distance.} In the discrete specialization $X=\mathbb{F}_q^N$ with $d_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $G$ acyclic, after replacing $G$ by the oriented reflexive transitive closure $G^{\preceq}$ of Corollary~1.4, the unnormalized distance $D_{X,G^{\preceq},P}:=N d_{X,G^{\preceq},P}$ coincides with the size of the hereditary closure of the support, yielding a poset/digraph \emph{sphere-packing bound} via the counting of lower ideals. Finally, we give a continuous analog of the construction, yielding a metric on $C([0,1],\mathbb C)$ through an explicit integral formula. These results unify and generalize several graph-based metrics used in coding theory while providing new design levers for mean-distance control.
item.dc:creator: Mahir Bilen Can, Shantanu Chakrabartty

item.title: Morse theory and moduli spaces of simple polylines and polygons
item.description: arXiv:2506.06781v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a smooth $d$-manifold $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^d$ if it admits a Lyapunov-Reeb function, i.e., a smooth map $f\colon M\to\mathbb R$ that is proper, lower-bounded, and possesses exactly one critical point. We further establish that the moduli spaces of simple polylines and positively oriented polygons with fixed or varying side lengths are diffeomorphic to Euclidean spaces, by explicitly constructing Lyapunov-Reeb functions on these spaces. This yields a refined resolution to the Carpenter's Rule Problem and settles a conjecture proposed by Gonz\'{a}lez and Sedano-Mendoza. In addition, we describe foliation structures of the moduli spaces and develop algorithms for the refolding problem.
item.dc:creator: Te Ba, Ze Zhou

item.title: An edge-spectral Erd\H{o}s-Stone-Simonovits theorem and its stability
item.description: arXiv:2508.15271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the extremal problem that relates the spectral radius $\lambda (G)$ of an $F$-free graph $G$ to its number of edges. Firstly, we prove that for any graph $F$ with chromatic number $\chi (F)=r+1\ge 3$, if $G$ is an $F$-free graph with $m$ edges, then $\lambda^2(G)\le {(1-\frac{1}{r} + o(1))2m}$. This provides a unified extension of both the Erd\H{o}s-Stone-Simonovits theorem and its vertex-spectral extension due to Nikiforov, and confirms a conjecture proposed by Li, Liu and Feng. We also establish the corresponding edge-spectral stability, showing that if $G$ is an $F$-free graph with $m$ edges with $\lambda^2(G) \ge (1- \frac{1}{r} - o(1))2m$, then $G$ differs from a complete bipartite graph by $o(m)$ edges when $r=2$, and $G$ differs from an $r$-partite Tur\'{a}n graph by $o(m)$ edges when $r\ge 3$. This extends both the classical Erd\H{o}s-Simonovits stability and the Nikiforov vertex-spectral stability. This edge-spectral stability theorem is the key ingredient in our companion work on the Brualdi-Hoffman-Tur\'{a}n problem for color-critical forbidden graphs. As an application of our method, we improve a result of Zhai, Lin and Shu by showing that if $\lambda (G)>\sqrt{m}$, then there exist two vertices in $G$ that have at least $\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{m} - O(1)$ common neighbors. The constant $\frac{1}{2}$ is best possible as witnessed by a random construction.
item.dc:creator: Yongtao Li, Hong Liu, Shengtong Zhang

item.title: Burling graphs in graphs with large chromatic number
item.description: arXiv:2510.19650v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph class is $\chi$-bounded if the only way to force large chromatic number in graphs from the class is by forming a large clique. In the 1970s, Erd\H{o}s conjectured that intersection graphs of straight-line segments in the plane are $\chi$-bounded, but this was disproved by Pawlik et al. (2014), who showed another way to force large chromatic number in this class -- by triangle-free graphs $B_k$ with $\chi(B_k)=k$ constructed by Burling (1965). This also disproved the celebrated conjecture of Scott (1997) that classes of graphs excluding induced subdivisions of a fixed graph are $\chi$-bounded. We prove that in broad classes of graphs excluding induced subdivisions of a fixed graph, including the increasingly more general classes of segment intersection graphs, string graphs, region intersection graphs, and hereditary classes of graphs with finite asymptotic dimension, large chromatic number can be forced only by large cliques or large graphs $B_k$. One corollary is that the hereditary closure of $\{B_k\colon k\geq 1\}$ forms a minimal hereditary graph class with unbounded chromatic number -- the second known graph class with this property after the class of complete graphs. Another corollary is that the decision variant of approximate coloring in the aforementioned graph classes can be solved in polynomial time by exhaustively searching for a sufficiently large clique or copy of $B_k$. We also discuss how our results along with some results of Chudnovsky, Scott, and Seymour on the existence of colorings can be turned into polynomial-time algorithms for the search variant of approximate coloring in string graphs (with intersection model in the input) and other aforementioned graph classes. Such an algorithm has not yet been known for any graph class that is not $\chi$-bounded.
item.dc:creator: Tara Abrishami, Marcin Bria\'nski, James Davies, Xiying Du, Jana Masa\v{r}\'ikov\'a, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Bartosz Walczak

item.title: Arithmetic Circuits and Neural Networks for Regular Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2511.02406v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that there exist uniform $(+,\times,/)$-circuits of size $O(n^3)$ to compute the basis generating polynomial of regular matroids on $n$ elements. By tropicalization, this implies that there exist uniform $(\max,+,-)$-circuits and ReLU neural networks of the same size for weighted basis maximization of regular matroids. As a consequence in linear programming theory, we obtain a first example where taking the difference of two extended formulations can be more efficient than the best known individual extended formulation for the base polytope of regular matroids of size $O(n^6)$ by Aprile and Fiorini. Such differences have recently been introduced as virtual extended formulations. The proof of our main result relies on a fine-tuned version of Seymour's decomposition of regular matroids which allows us to identify and maintain graphic substructures to which we can apply a local version of the star-mesh transformation.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Hertrich, Stefan Kober, Georg Loho

item.title: On set-like sunflower-free families of subspaces over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2605.12232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Erd\H{o}s--Rado sunflower problem admits two natural analogues in finite vector spaces, corresponding to two different ways of generalising the set-theoretic notion of a sunflower. The first, used by Ihringer and Kupavskii [FFA 110 (2026) 102746], requires the petals to be in general position over the kernel; the second, used in the subspace codes literature (cf.\ Etzion--Raviv [DAM 186 (2015) 87-97], Blokhuis--De Boeck--D'haeseleer [DCC 90 (2022) 2101-2111]), requires only that the kernel equals the pairwise intersection of distinct petals. We refer to the second version as a \emph{set-like sunflower}, following Blokhuis, De Boeck and D'haeseleer. In this note, we focus on the set-like setting. {We first observe by illustrations that general-position sunflower-freeness does not imply set-like sunflower-freeness.} We then present a construction of set-like $s$-sunflower-free families of $k$-spaces \revised{in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ for $\lceil(n+1)/2\rceil \leq k \leq n-1$, of size $q^{n-k}$ (and $q^{n-k}+1$ for even $q$),} based on a manipulated version of the lifting construction; to our knowledge, this is the first systematic construction tailored to this setting. Finally, we compare the size of the construction with the exact optimum for small parameters, computed by exhaustive search.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Otal

item.title: On balanced subfamilies of maximum complement-free families in the middle layer of the Boolean lattice
item.description: arXiv:2606.16172v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study balanced subfamilies of the middle layer $\binom{[2n]}{n}$ of the Boolean lattice $2^{[2n]}$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ is said to be balanced if every element in $[2n]$ appears in the same number of members of $\mathcal{F}$. A balanced subfamily of size 2 is exactly a complementary pair $\{A,[2n]\setminus A\}$, and therefore a family with no balanced subfamily of size $2$ has at most $\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n}$ members. We show that for every $k\geq 1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, this maximum size is compatible with delaying the smallest size of a balanced subfamily until $2k+2$. More precisely, there exists a family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ of size $\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n}$ with no balanced subfamilies of sizes $2,4,\ldots,2k$, but with a balanced subfamily of size $2k+2$. The proof is constructive and uses a general lifting from simple games to self-dual selectors in the middle layer. This provides an efficient constructive proof of a recent conjecture of Moss and Pedersen.
item.dc:creator: Sa'ul A. Blanco

item.title: The chain replacement of a poset flow
item.description: arXiv:2607.11639v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the chain replacement of a poset flow: it is obtained by considering the simplicial nerves of the posets of strictly increasing chains in the given poset, ordered by refinement. It maps posets to q-cofibrant flows and inclusions of posets to q-cofibrations. Using the combinatorial properties of the chain replacement, we prove that pushouts along the chain replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets induce trivial h-cofibrations on spaces of execution paths between states of the original flow. By introducing the Hurewicz model structure on flows (or H-model structure), we deduce the same property for any q-cofibrant replacement of an order-reflecting inclusion of posets.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Gaucher

item.title: HJ numbers revisited
item.description: arXiv:2607.14732v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We improve the bounds on the Hales-Jewett numbers to a tower of exponentiations. Earlier it was $WaW$ (that is, iterations of towers which are themselves iterated exponentiations). We improve the inductive step there (induction on the size of the alphabet, $|\Lambda|$) to 2-exponentiations, instead of towers. In the longer work in typing, (A) We present this inductive step as a partition theorem in its own right; (but in this preliminary version we make it just serve the bound on HJ numbers). (B) We shall deal with the density version of Hales-Jewett with similar bound. We are also dealing with the Graham-Rothschild Theorem and the Affine Ramsey Theorem and the polynomial case, and give background.
item.dc:creator: Saharon Shelah

item.title: Exact Clique Counts in Graphs with a Forbidden Tree
item.description: arXiv:2608.25746v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a fixed tree $T$ on $t$ vertices, let $\ex(n,K_r,T)$ denote the maximum number of $r$-cliques in an $n$-vertex $T$-free graph. Write $n=\alpha(t-1)+\beta$ with $0\le\beta<t-1$.
