A conjecture proposed in extremal-graph form by Alon and Shikhelman~\cite{alon2016}, later stated explicitly as an exact clique-counting formula by Gerbner and Palmer~\cite{GP2026}, asserts that \[ \ex(n,K_r,T)=\alpha\binom{t-1}{r}+\binom\beta r, \] with the extremal construction given by the vertex disjoint union of $\alpha$ copies of $K_{t-1}$ and a graph with $\beta$ vertices. This paper proves this conjecture for every $n$ and for every tree $T$ whenever $C\log t\le r\le t-1$ and $t$ is sufficiently large, where $C$ is an absolute constant. This lowers the previously known general threshold $r\ge\lceil(2t-1)/3\rceil$, which is linear in $t$ to logarithmic order. The paper also proves the conjecture for every $3\le r\le t-1$ when at least $\lceil(t-3)/2\rceil$ leaves of $T$ have a common neighbor, and this extends the known results for stars and double stars.
item.dc:creator: XiaoJun Zhao, YueJian Peng

item.title: On high-girth layered graphs of large Tur\'an density in a hypercube
item.description: arXiv:2608.30544v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a graph $H$, let $\operatorname{ex}(Q_n, H)$ be the largest number of edges in a subgraph of the hypercube $Q_n$ of dimension $n$ that contains no subgraph isomorphic to $H$. We define $\pi_\square(H)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{ex}(Q_n,H)/|E(Q_n)|$ as the Tur\'an density of $H$ in the hypercube. Although determining $\pi_\square(H)$ for general $H$ remains widely open, Conlon found a large class of graphs with zero Tur\'an density in a hypercube. In this note, we address the case when $\pi_{\square} (H)>0$. If a graph $H$ cannot be embedded in an edge layer of a hypercube, then $\pi_{\square} (H)\geq 1/2$, as can be seen by taking every other edge layer of $Q_n$. Previously known examples of layered graphs of positive Tur\'an density in a hypercube include graphs containing cycles of length $6$ or $10$, as well as examples of girth $8$. Also, to the best of our knowledge, all previously known examples of graphs with Tur\'an densities arbitrarily close to one are not layered. We show that for every $g \geq 3$, there are layered graphs of girth greater than $g$ whose Tur\'an densities in a hypercube are arbitrarily close to one. Moreover, these graphs have an induced embedding into an edge layer of a hypercube.
item.dc:creator: Maria Axenovich, Marko Peji\'c

item.title: The Multiorbital Bivariate Chromatic Polynomial: A Subgroup-Lattice Refinement
item.description: arXiv:2609.01866v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomial F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}P_{\Gamma/h}(x,y), which aggregates the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials associated with all subgroups of a finite group acting on a graph. We derive the equivalent element-wise representation F_\Gamma(G;x,y) = \sum_{g\in G}c_G(g)P_{\Gamma/g}(x,y), where c_G(g) = \sum_{\langle g\rangle\leq H\leq G}\frac{1}{|H|}. The coefficient function depends only on the cyclic subgroup generated by the element and is constant on conjugacy classes. This yields decompositions by cyclic subgroups and conjugacy classes and an interpretation in terms of the incidence algebra of the subgroup lattice. After normalization, the coefficients define a probability distribution obtained by choosing a subgroup uniformly and then an element uniformly from that subgroup. We also establish diagonal multiplicativity for disjoint unions and a weighted cycle-index expression for edgeless graphs. A further contribution concerns the distinguishing power of the orbital bivariate chromatic polynomial. We answer a question of Dohmen and Lange-Geisler affirmatively by exhibiting two non-isomorphic graphs, P_3 and K_2 \mathbin{\dot\cup} K_1 under C_2-actions, with identical orbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. The two actions nevertheless have different multiorbital bivariate chromatic polynomials. Thus the multiorbital polynomial is not determined by the orbital bivariate polynomial, whereas the converse question remains open.
item.dc:creator: Melanie Gerling

item.title: Unique Minimizers for Permanents, Mixed Discriminants, and Log-concave Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.21083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The permanent and mixed discriminant of positive matrices are classic problems for which we do not expect an efficient algorithm for exact computation. Thus much work has been done to understand how well we can bound and approximately compute these quantities. One line of research in this area begins with the results of the first author, where van der Waerden lower bounds of $\frac{n!}{n^n}$ are proven for doubly stochastic inputs for both problems, using a simple proof via stable polynomials. Along with the bound itself, the same techniques are used to show that the permanent and mixed discriminant are uniquely minimized at a certain natural symmetric input. In this paper, we generalize those results in two ways. First, we extend the unique minimization results beyond doubly stochastic inputs to other marginals which are near doubly stochastic. This yields the first such unique minimization results for the mixed discriminant beyond the doubly stochastic case. We also discuss why one cannot hope similar results to hold in general for all marginals. Second, we extend the unique minimization result for real stable polynomials to strongly log-concave (aka Lorentzian) polynomials in the doubly stochastic case. This captures an analogous previous result on unique minimization for the mixed volume. Finally, we discuss various open problems related to these results.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Gurvits, Jonathan Leake

item.title: There Are No Nontrivial Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
item.description: arXiv:2609.23128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In his pioneering work from 1973, Delsarte conjectured that the Johnson scheme J$(n,w)$ admits no nontrivial perfect codes. Although related existence problems have been resolved in several other association schemes, the problem in the Johnson scheme remained open. We prove Delsarte's conjecture: no nontrivial e-perfect code exists in any Johnson scheme. The proof combines divisibility properties of balls in the scheme, bounds on the strength of designs associated with perfect codes, the roots of Lloyd polynomials, and explicit results on primes and linear forms in logarithms.
item.dc:creator: Tuvi Etzion, Xiande Zhang, Wenjie Zhong

item.title: Disproof of a Conjectured Upper Bound for the Davenport Constant
item.description: arXiv:2609.29878v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G= C_{n_1}\oplus\cdots\oplus C_{n_r}$ be a finite abelian group with $1<n_1\mid\cdots\mid n_r$, and let $\rr(G)=r$ denote its rank. The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ is the least integer $\ell$ such that every sequence of $\ell$ elements of $G$ contains a nonempty zero-sum subsequence, and $\DD^*(G)=1+\sum_{i=1}^r(n_i-1)$ is its classical lower bound. A long-standing conjecture asserts that $\DD(G)\le\DD^*(G)+\rr(G)-1$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture. More strongly, we prove that $\sup_{\rr(G)=r}\bigl(\DD(G)-\DD^*(G)\bigr)=\infty$ for every fixed $r\ge5$. Thus the classical lower bound does not approximate the Davenport constant within an additive error depending only on the rank. More precisely, our construction gives $\delta(C_m^{r-4}\oplus C_{3m}^3\oplus C_{6m})\ge m$ for all integers $r\ge5$ and $m\ge2$. Consequently, the least rank $r_0$ for unbounded Davenport excess $\DD(G)-\DD^*(G)$ satisfies $3\le r_0\le5$. Our result also disproves the Narkiewicz--\'{S}liwa conjecture of 1982 \cite{NS82} on the Narkiewicz constant, arising in algebraic number theory from the quantitative study of algebraic integers with unique factorization. The same amplification of the Davenport excess yields counterexamples to Girard's conjecture \cite[Conjecture 1.2]{Girard08} on the cross numbers of long zero-sum-free sequences. As a further main result, we establish the uniform upper bound $$\DD(G)\le\frac{16}{5}\rr(G)\exp(G)$$ for every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$. The classical estimate of van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk \cite{vEBK69} gives $\DD(G)\le\exp(G)\left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \le\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$. Our bound removes the logarithmic factor $\log\exp(G)$ from this classical estimate, and replaces it with the absolute constant $16/5$.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang

item.title: There is no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph
item.description: arXiv:2609.37978v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph is $K_3$-irregular if its vertices belong to pairwise distinct numbers of triangles. We prove that no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists, settling the last unresolved case. Following the initial discovery of such graphs for regularities $r \in \{10,11,12\}$ (Stevanovi'c et al., 2024), our previous work (Hak et al., 2025) showed that no such graphs exist for $r \le 7$, provided the first example for $r=9$, and proved that any $8$-regular candidate must have between $17$ and $22$ vertices. We exclude these possible orders for $r=8$ by combining careful analysis of triangle degrees with integer linear programming techniques. Meanwhile, a recent construction (Zhang, 2026) established that regular $K_3$-irregular graphs do exist for all $r \ge 9$. Together with our results, this establishes that an $r$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists if and only if $r\geq 9$.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko, Andrii Serdiuk

item.title: Schur positivity of the lattices $\mathbf m\times\mathbf n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.01617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the product of chains $\mathbf m\times\mathbf n$ is not Schur positive whenever $n\ge4$ and $m\ge3n-1$. Writing $m=n+k$, we exhibit a negative Schur coefficient indexed by $(2n+k-1,2n+k-3,\ldots,k+5,k,k,4)$ and evaluate it explicitly as $(n-2)!$ times a polynomial of degree three in $k$. Together with earlier results, this establishes the two-case interpretation of the conjecture of Li, Qiu, Yang, and Zhang: these products are not Schur positive when $n=2$ and $m\ge8$, or when $n\ge3$ and $m\ge n+5$.
item.dc:creator: Kai Zhang

item.title: On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins
item.description: arXiv:2610.13798v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For $X \subseteq V(D)$, the inversion of $X$ in $D$ is the oriented graph that is obtained via changing the direction of all edges which have both endpoints in $X$. The inversion number of $D$, $\operatorname{inv}(D)$, is the minimum number of inversions necessary in order to remove all cycles from $D$. A dijoin $D_1 \to D_2$ is the oriented graph obtained by taking disjoint copies of $D_1,D_2$ and adding edges from all $v \in V(D_1)$ to each $u \in V(D_2)$. It was conjectured by Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1) + \operatorname{inv}(D_2)$ for all $D_1, D_2$. This was disproved by simultaneous constructions of various $D_1$, $D_2$ with $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) = \operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2)-1$. However, no known constructions achieved more than this gain of 1. Moreover, all of the constructions exploit a gap of 1 between $\operatorname{inv}(D)$ and the minimum rank of a family of related matrices, a gap that can never be more than 1, suggesting that perhaps something close to the original conjecture might be true. We prove that in fact additivity fails badly. In particular, for all $\varepsilon>0$ we show that there exist tournaments $D_1$, $D_2$ with arbitrarily large inversion numbers such that $\operatorname{inv}(D_1 \to D_2) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2} +\varepsilon\right)(\operatorname{inv}(D_1)+\operatorname{inv}(D_2))$.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Behague, Jack Cromwell

item.title: Symmetric, rational and infinitely many $(23_4)$ configurations, and the end of the existence problem for geometric $(n_4)$ configurations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14099v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A geometric $(n_4)$ configuration is a set of $n$ points and $n$ lines in the real projective plane such that every point lies on exactly four of the lines and every line contains exactly four of the points. The question of which $n$ admit such a configuration was posed by Gr\"unbaum in 2000, and successive work of Bokowski, Gr\"unbaum, Schewe, Pilaud and Cuntz settled every case but $n=23$. We settle this last case by bounding the symmetry of such configurations and classifying the most symmetric ones exactly. We prove that for every prime $n\equiv3\pmod4$ the group of projective symmetries of a geometric $(n_4)$ configuration has order at most four, explaining why symmetric constructions failed at $n=23$, and the same argument bounds the symmetry of $(n_5)$ configurations for primes $n\not\equiv1\pmod5$. Reducing the Klein four-group case to 4021 bilinear polynomial systems and solving all of them exactly with Gr\"obner bases, we show that exactly two $(23_4)$ configurations reach this bound up to projective equivalence and that there are no others even over $\mathbb{C}$. Both are self-polar; the first has integer coordinates and the second is defined over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{17})$ but not over $\mathbb{Q}$. Consequently geometric $(n_4)$ configurations exist if and only if $n\ge18$ and $n\ne19$. The same classification recovers Cuntz's $(22_4)$ and $(26_4)$ configurations and finds three new combinatorial types at $n=22$ and $94$ at $n=26$. Among self-polar $(23_4)$ configurations with a single involution we find $50$ more, defined over number fields of degree at most $7$. Four of them deform in one-parameter families, and computing three of these exactly, one birational to the modular curve $X_1(11)$, we prove that there are infinitely many geometric $(23_4)$ configurations, among them infinitely many with rational coordinates that are self-polar and have no projective symmetry.

item.title: The $\lambda$-chain condition for unit interval determinantal fiber rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.15971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that certain finite partially ordered sets arising from unit interval determinantal facet ideals satisfy the $\lambda$-chain condition. In addition, their applications to commutative algebra are briefly discussed.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Sora Miyashita

item.title: Quality control in sublinear time: a case study via random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2508.16531v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many algorithms are designed to work well on average over inputs. But when such an algorithm is run on an arbitrary input, the question arises: Can we trust the algorithm on this input? This question is especially relevant in network science, where algorithms for theoretical random graph models are often applied to individual real-world networks. We identify a new class of algorithmic problems addressing this, which we call "Quality Control Problems." These problems are specified by a "quality function" $\rho$ and a distribution $D$ such that, with high probability, a sample drawn from $D$ is "high quality," meaning its $\rho$-value is near $1$. The goal is to accept most inputs $x \sim D$ and reject potentially adversarially generated inputs $x$ with $\rho(x)$ far from $1$. In this work, we consider the sublinear version of the quality control problem, where $D \in \Delta(\{0,1\}^N)$ and the goal is to solve the $(D,\rho)$-quality problem with $o(N)$ queries and time. As a case study, we consider random graphs, i.e., $D = G_{n,p}$ (and $N = \binom{n}2$), and the $k$-clique count function $\rho_k := C_k(G)/\mathbb{E}_{G' \sim G_{n,p}}[C_k(G')]$, where $C_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-cliques in $G$. In suitable parameter ranges, worst-case approximate $k$-clique counting requires $p^{-\Omega(k^2)}$ queries. In contrast, we show that the quality control problem for $G_{n,p}$ (with $n\geq p^{-ck}$ for some constant $c$) with respect to $\rho_k$ can be tested with $p^{-O(k)}$ queries and time, showing quality control is provably superpolynomially more efficient in this setting. More generally, for a motif $H$ of maximum degree $\Delta(H)$, we show that the corresponding quality control problem can be solved with $p^{-O(\Delta(H))}$ queries and running time.
item.dc:creator: Cassandra Marcussen, Ronitt Rubinfeld, Madhu Sudan

item.title: Metric geometry for ranking-based voting: Tools for learning electoral structure
item.description: arXiv:2602.10293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we develop the metric geometry of ranking statistics, proving that the two major permutation distances in the statistics literature -- Kendall tau and Spearman footrule -- extend naturally to incomplete rankings with both coordinate embeddings and graph realizations. This gives us a unifying framework that allows us to connect popular topics in computational social choice: metric preferences (and metric distortion), polarization, and proportionality. As an important application, the metric structure enables efficient identification of blocs of voters and slates of their preferred candidates. Since the definitions work for partial ballots, we can execute the methods not only on synthetic elections, but on a suite of real-world elections. This gives us robust clustering methods that often produce an identical grouping of voters -- even though one family of methods is based on a Condorcet-consistent ranking rule while the other is not.
item.dc:creator: Moon Duchin, Kristopher Tapp

item.title: Hyperplane arrangements with non-formal Milnor fibers
item.description: arXiv:2603.07301v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Each complex hyperplane arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ gives rise to a Milnor fibration of its complement. Building on work of Zuber, we give a combinatorial sufficient condition for the Milnor fiber $F(\mathcal{A})$ to be non-$1$-formal, expressed in terms of the multinet structure on $\mathcal{A}$, and use it to produce an infinite family of monomial arrangements $\mathcal{A}(3k,3k,3)$ with non-formal Milnor fibers. We also review the relevant background on cohomology jump loci, formality, and the topology of Milnor fibers of arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu

item.title: The complexity of smooth words over binary alphabets
item.description: arXiv:2603.10733v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Smooth sequences over an alphabet of positive integers $\{a,b\}$ are sequences that are infinitely derivable, the emblematic example being the Oldenburger-Kolakoski sequence $\kappa$ over $\{1,2\}$. The main way to study their language is to consider a finite version of smooth sequences called smooth words. In this paper we prove that the smooth words are exactly the factors of smooth sequences and we make progress towards the conjecture that the complexity of smooth words over $\{a,b\}$ grows like $\Theta\left(n^{\log(a+b)/\log((a+b)/2)}\right)$: we prove the lower bound over any alphabet and the upper bound over even alphabets, and we improve the known upper bound over odd and mixed alphabets. We also provide a dichotomy that links the language, the morphicity and the factor complexity of $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Julien Cassaigne, Rapha\"el Henry

item.title: Classifying Prime Character Degree Graphs With Eight Vertices
item.description: arXiv:2603.15851v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, an effort is made to classify which prime character degree graphs having eight vertices occur for some finite solvable group. To approach this, we compile known results and constructions from the literature which are used to develop a general algorithm to begin classifying graphs of any order. We then apply the algorithm to the graphs of order eight. Of the 12,346 non-isomorphic graphs with eight vertices, 1,229 are disconnected and are fully classified. Meanwhile, thirty-seven of the 11,117 non-isomorphic connected graphs are shown to occur; thirty-four of which are constructed via joins of smaller graphs and three of which have diameter three. Fifty-eight graphs are shown not to occur, several of which fall into previously studied families, while the classification of 204 graphs is still unknown.

item.title: Non-convex polytopes realizing kissing contact graphs in dimensions 5-7
item.description: arXiv:2609.12640v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Each of the 12 known conjecturally optimal kissing configurations in dimensions 5, 6, and 7 carries a contact-graph polytope: a polytope whose vertices are the configuration points and whose edges are exactly its contacts. Eight of these polytopes are non-convex and distinct from their convex hulls, which include longer edges. Each polytope is radial about the sphere's center: its boundary meets every ray from the center exactly once. It is the unique radial polytope with those vertices and edges. Seven of the nine non-lattice configurations carry polytopes constructed from the lattice contact polytope in the same dimension by splitting some facets and reassembling the pieces. This split-and-reassemble construction describes the configurations by facets rather than by layers. The fold angles of the reassembled facets explain the inner products $1/(10-n)$, giving $1/5$, $1/4$, and $1/3$ in dimensions 5, 6, and 7, respectively. The contact graphs of all 12 configurations are infinitesimally rigid. We also prove that $Q_5$ and $R_5$ are infinitesimally jammed, extending the 10 previously established cases to all 12 configurations. All mathematical computations use exact arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Self

item.title: Structural Properties of DomiRank Centrality: Symmetry Axioms, an Entropy Bound, and Spectral Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.00107v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: DomiRank is a node-importance algorithm for unweighted networks, defined by a dynamical model governed by a competition-strength parameter, a dominance threshold, and a decay rate. We establish three structural results. First, on symmetry. Automorphism-related vertices share the same DomiRank value, and a graph whose values are pairwise distinct must be asymmetric. The orbit count bounds the number of distinct values, and regular and vertex-transitive graphs admit closed forms. Second, on entropy. The maximum of the DomiRank entropy over connected graphs, log_2 N, is attained if and only if the graph is regular. The initial entropy derivative is the degree-log-degree edge covariance, making the decrease rigorous near vanishing competition for structurally disassortative graphs, and an assortative counterexample shows it does not extend to all graphs; a sufficient-condition theorem and a refined conjecture cover the rest. Third, on spectrum. The normalized distribution is sigma-invariant if and only if the degree vector is an adjacency-matrix eigenvector. The parameter sigma interpolates continuously between degree and smallest-eigenvector centrality within the resolvent (Bonacich-type) family, its sensitivity being a second-order suppression operator on the degree vector. Graph transformations are also characterized, including the m-product. Experiments on four real networks and synthetic families up to 10^4 vertices confirm the interpolation and exhibit monotone entropy decrease, continuous ranking interpolation, decaying positive fraction and ranking reversals; where the positive fraction has decayed far from one, the limit describes the solution vector rather than the induced ranking. DomiRank is thus a tunable complement to principal-eigenvector centrality. A companion study quantifies how much of its task-level edge over a degree baseline survives degree correction.
item.dc:creator: Yingying Zhang, Chengye Zhao

item.title: The theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations of groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15826v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by recent work on $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations by Kreher, Li, and Stinson (Designs, Codes and Cryptography, 2026), we introduce and systematically investigate $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations as combinatorial structures with prescribed representation multiplicities. Such a factorization consists of two subsets of a finite group whose products represent each nonidentity element exactly $\lambda$ times and the identity exactly $\mu$ times. These structures generalize $\lambda$-fold near-factorizations and provide a common framework for several families arising in combinatorial design theory, including strong external difference families with two equal-sized subsets, as well as binary sequence pairs with two-level correlation. Their associated $\{0,1\}$-matrices satisfy the Bridges-Ryser equation $XY=\lambda(J-I)+\mu I$, linking the factorization problem to a classical matrix framework for combinatorial designs. We establish the foundational theory of $(\lambda,\mu)$-fold factorizations, provide two general constructions, and prove several nonexistence results for finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Donald L. Kreher, Shuxing Li, Douglas R. Stinson
